title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing for Minimum Inhibitory Concentration of Antibiotics
author: Barnes V, Heithoff, et al.

steps.title: Identify pathogen
steps.instruction: Obtain pathogen identification from the clinical laboratory or determine it by standard identification methods such as PCR, microarray, or immunology.

steps.title: Select antibiotics and test ranges
steps.instruction: Choose antibiotics according to CLSI/EUCAST guidelines, retrieve the MIC distribution for the selected pathogen from the EUCAST MIC repository, view the predicted susceptibility profile, and define a continuous range of ten two‑fold dilutions that span the clinical breakpoints; calculate twice the highest concentration of each antibiotic to use for stock preparation.

substeps.instruction: Access the EUCAST MIC distribution repository (https://mic.eucast.org/search/).
Select the pathogen from the drop‑down list.
Select each antibiotic and view its predicted susceptibility profile.
Choose ten 2‑fold dilutions that encompass the clinical breakpoints (if available).
Calculate 2 × the highest concentration within the chosen range for each antibiotic.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each antibiotic in the solvent and at the concentration listed in Table 1, vortex, heat to 37 °C if needed, agitate piperacillin for 3 min, filter‑sterilize if required, and store at 4 °C protected from light for up to two weeks (or at –80 °C for powder/sub‑aliquots of unstable drugs).

substeps.instruction: Store deionized H₂O at 4 °C; store drug powders at –80 °C; store all other sub‑aliquots at 4 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Culture bacteria in CAMHB and DMEM
steps.instruction: Inoculate the identified isolate into cation‑adjusted Mueller‑Hinton broth (CAMHB) and Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium (DMEM) and incubate for 18 h at 37 °C (CAMHB in ambient atmosphere; DMEM in 5 % CO₂) for three biological replicates.

steps.title: Determine bacterial concentration
steps.instruction: Serially dilute each 18 h culture 1:10 (5–7 dilutions), plate 100 µL of the last three dilutions on the appropriate bacteriological agar, incubate 18 h at 37 °C, count colonies, and calculate CFU mL⁻¹; alternatively estimate CFU mL⁻¹ from OD₆₀₀.

steps.title: Prepare 2 × 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹ inoculum
steps.instruction: Dilute the overnight cultures in the respective medium to obtain a bacterial suspension of 2 × 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹ (double the target 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹) for use in the microdilution assay.

steps.title: Set up 96‑well microdilution plate
steps.instruction: Dispense antibiotic serial dilutions (ten 2‑fold concentrations) into columns 1‑10 of a standard 96‑well plate; add a positive‑control well with bacteria only in column 11 and a negative‑control well with media only in column 12. A standard plate can accommodate eight antibiotics (8 × [10 concentrations + 1 positive + 1 negative]).

steps.title: Add bacterial inoculum to wells
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the 2 × 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹ bacterial suspension to each well containing antibiotic dilutions to achieve a final inoculum of ~10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹ per well.

steps.title: Incubate MIC plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates for 20 h at 37 °C; for CAMHB plates keep in ambient atmosphere, for DMEM plates maintain 5 % CO₂, standing.

steps.title: Verify inoculum after incubation
steps.instruction: Serially dilute a 100 µL aliquot of the inoculum ~10³‑fold, plate 100 µL on LB agar (or pathogen‑specific agar: TSB for E. faecium/S. aureus; THB + 2 % YE for S. pneumoniae), incubate 18 h at 37 °C, and confirm the CFU mL⁻¹ is within 3‑fold of the target 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Read MIC values
steps.instruction: Determine the minimum inhibitory concentration as the lowest antibiotic concentration that shows no visible bacterial growth.

steps.title: Interpret MIC against breakpoints
steps.instruction: Compare each MIC to CLSI/EUCAST clinical breakpoints to classify the isolate as susceptible (S), intermediate (I), or resistant (R).

steps.title: Isolate bacteria on agar (alternate protocol)
steps.instruction: Plate the pathogen on appropriate bacteriological agar as described in the standard protocol and incubate under the required conditions.

steps.title: Culture in pooled human serum or urine
steps.instruction: Inoculate one colony per replicate into 0.5 mL of undiluted pooled human donor serum or urine (three biological replicates) and incubate 18 h at 37 °C; for serum maintain 5 % CO₂ standing, for urine incubate with shaking at 225 rpm ambient. Apply pathogen‑specific modifications: A. baumannii – heat‑inactivate serum at 56 °C for 30 min then supplement with 40 % v/v CAMHB; S. pneumoniae – supplement with 30 % v/v THB, inoculate 5 colonies, incubate 4 h at 37 °C (serum 5 % CO₂ standing; urine ambient standing).

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic dilutions for fluids
steps.instruction: Make antibiotic serial dilutions in the same fluid used for bacterial growth, adjusting the medium as follows: A. baumannii – heat‑inactivated serum + 40 % v/v CAMHB; E. faecium – serum or urine + 30 % v/v TSB; S. pneumoniae – serum or urine + 30 % v/v THB.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial inoculum in fluids
steps.instruction: Vortex the overnight cultures for 15 s at maximum speed to disrupt aggregates, then dilute to 2 × 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹ in the respective fluid supplemented with 30 % v/v LB (or the pathogen‑specific supplement); vortex 5 s between dilutions; withdraw 100 µL to a microfuge tube and verify CFU mL⁻¹ is within 3‑fold of target.

steps.title: Incubate serum/urine MIC plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the microtiter plates for 20 h at 37 °C standing; for serum maintain 5 % CO₂, for urine keep ambient atmosphere.

steps.title: Confirm inoculum in fluids
steps.instruction: As in the standard protocol, verify the 2 × 10⁶ CFU mL⁻¹ inoculum by plating diluted samples and confirming counts within 3‑fold of the target.

steps.title: Determine MIC in fluids
steps.instruction: Read MIC as described in the standard protocol (lowest concentration with no visible growth).

steps.title: Interpret fluid MICs
steps.instruction: Interpret MIC values using CLSI/EUCAST clinical breakpoints as in the standard protocol.

description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) to existing medications is one of the biggest challenges facing public healthcare.2 Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) is used to determine the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), the standard measurement of antibiotic activity. MICs define the clinical breakpoint, the concentration of antibiotic used to indicate whether an infection with a particular bacterial isolate is likely to be treatable in a patient. Clinical breakpoints are used by clinical microbiological laboratories to define patient isolates as susceptible (S), intermediate (I), or resistant (R) to a panel of antibiotics. Thus, the MIC assay is the gold standard for guiding physician treatment practices. This protocol evaluates MIC values of clinically relevant antibiotics against bacterial isolates cultured in standard bacteriologic medium (cation-adjusted Mueller-Hinton broth [CAMHB]) and in mammalian cell culture medium (Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium [DMEM]).1,3,4 Before commencing AST, it is essential to prepare the required reagents (media, buffers, antibiotics) (Table 1); identify the pathogen to be tested; select antibiotic concentration test ranges; and determine pathogen growth conditions to obtain adequate densities for reliable MIC determination.1.Identify Pathogen (ID).a.Obtain ID from clinical laboratory or determine by standard ID methods (PCR, microarray, immunology).2.Determine antibiotic panel and concentration ranges.a.Select antibiotics with guidance from Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) and European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing (EUCAST), or institutional policy.b.Determine MIC test range.i.Access the EUCAST MIC distribution repository5; https://mic.eucast.org/search/.ii.Select pathogen from the drop-down list.iii.Select antibiotic and view predicted susceptibility profile for each pathogen (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus susceptibility to ciprofloxacin) (Figure 1).Figure 1Antibiotic test rangeEUCAST c
